balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

onlineSameStore.title: Online sales mix and same-store sales growth
onlineSameStore.content:
Online sales % is the share of group sales transacted online rather than in a physical store; same-store sales growth (like-for-like) strips out the effect of opening or closing stores, isolating demand at the stores that traded in both periods.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the store count has been shrinking (88 → 85 over FY2024-FY2025), so total revenue growth alone would conflate closures with genuine demand -- same-store growth is the cleaner read on whether the remaining estate is getting healthier, and online mix shows how much of any growth is channel shift rather than more spend.

What to watch:

  • Negative same-store growth even while online mix rises (store traffic being cannibalised, not grown)
  • Online % plateauing, which would cap the operating-leverage case for lower store capex
  • Only interim periods are disclosed here -- there is no full-year same-store figure in the filings

storeCount.title: Store count
storeCount.content:
The number of trading stores in The Warehouse format at each reporting date.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the estate has been rationalised (88 → 85 stores FY2024-FY2025), so revenue and EBITDA trends elsewhere on this dashboard partly reflect a smaller footprint, not just weaker per-store trading -- read this alongside same-store sales growth, not the headline Revenue chart alone.

What to watch:

  • Whether closures are concentrated in underperforming sites (margin-accretive) or broad-based (demand problem)
  • Store count stabilising versus continuing to fall

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For The Warehouse Group Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
